scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY-Inland): Stocking of fingerlings in reservoir - Gujarat
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme aims to enhance fish production in India through various interventions. 

The PMMSY is designed to bring about a significant increase in fish production, thereby contributing to the overall goal of achieving self-sufficiency in fish production. 

The scheme is particularly focused on the sustainable development of the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY is implemented with an investment of ₹20,050 crores over a period of five years. 

The scheme is expected to increase fish production to 22 million metric tons by 2024-25. 

One of the key objectives of the PMMSY is to provide financial assistance for the stocking of fingerlings in reservoirs. 

This initiative aims to enhance the availability of quality fish seed. 

The stocking of fingerlings is crucial for maintaining the ecological balance in water bodies. 

In Gujarat, the PMMSY focuses on the stocking of fingerlings in various reservoirs. 

The state has a rich tradition of fishing and aquaculture. 

Gujarat contributes significantly to the overall fish production in India. 

The PMMSY aims to further boost this contribution by enhancing fish farming practices. 

The benefits of the scheme include increased fish production and improved livelihoods for fishermen. 

Fishermen and fish farmers can receive financial assistance under this scheme. 

The assistance provided can be up to 60% of the project cost for individual beneficiaries. 

For groups or cooperatives, the assistance can go up to 80% of the project cost. 

The financial assistance is subject to a maximum limit of ₹5 lakh for individual beneficiaries. 

For groups, the maximum limit can be ₹20 lakh. 

Eligibility for the PMMSY includes individuals and groups engaged in fishing and aquaculture. 

Beneficiaries must be registered with the Fisheries Department of Gujarat. 

The age limit for applicants is typically 18 years and above. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested beneficiaries must visit the official website of the Fisheries Department of Gujarat. 

They need to fill out the application form available online. 

The application form requires details such as personal information, project details, and bank account information. 

Beneficiaries must also submit supporting documents. 

These documents include identity proof, address proof, and bank account details. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the Fisheries Department. 

If approved, beneficiaries will receive a sanction order. 

The disbursement of funds is made directly to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries. 

The timeline for the application process can vary. 

Typically, the review and approval process takes about 30 to 45 days. 

The stocking of fingerlings is usually done during the monsoon season. 

This is when water levels in reservoirs are optimal for fish growth. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the importance of sustainable fishing practices. 

It encourages the use of environmentally friendly methods in aquaculture. 

The scheme aims to create awareness among fishermen about sustainable practices. 

The implementing authority for the PMMSY in Gujarat is the Fisheries Department. 

The department is responsible for the overall implementation and monitoring of the scheme. 

Contact details for the Fisheries Department can be found on their official website. 

The PMMSY also includes provisions for capacity building and training for fishermen. 

Workshops and training sessions are organized to educate beneficiaries about modern fishing techniques. 

The scheme aims to empower women in the fisheries sector as well. 

Special provisions are made to encourage women's participation in aquaculture. 

The PMMSY is part of a larger initiative to promote the Blue Revolution in India. 

The Blue Revolution aims to increase fish production and improve the livelihoods of those dependent on fisheries. 

The scheme also focuses on the development of infrastructure for fisheries. 

This includes the construction of fish landing centers and cold storage facilities. 

The PMMSY has a significant impact on rural employment. 

It is expected to create around 15 lakh direct and indirect jobs in the fisheries sector. 

The scheme also aims to increase the income of fishermen by 30%. 

The PMMSY is aligned with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders in the fisheries sector. 

It is seen as a crucial step towards achieving sustainable fisheries in India. 

The PMMSY also promotes the use of technology in fish farming. 

Digital platforms are being developed to provide information and support to fishermen. 

The scheme encourages the establishment of fish feed manufacturing units. 

This is to ensure the availability of quality feed for aquaculture. 

The PMMSY also includes provisions for research and development in fisheries. 

This is aimed at improving fish breeding and farming techniques. 

The overall goal of the PMMSY is to make India a global leader in fish production. 

By enhancing fish farming practices, the scheme aims to meet the growing demand for fish. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive initiative that addresses various aspects of the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable fisheries ecosystem in India. 

The scheme is expected to have a long-lasting impact on the livelihoods of millions of fishermen. 

Through the PMMSY, the government is committed to transforming the fisheries sector in India. 

The stocking of fingerlings in reservoirs is just one of the many initiatives under this scheme. 

The PMMSY represents a significant investment in the future of India's fisheries. 

It aims to ensure food security and improve the nutritional standards of the population. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to the development of the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY is a vital step towards achieving sustainable development goals in India.
